notes: Fifteen source-anchored first-sentence practice cues support the C-13 seven-pattern grammar before graded Listen. All existing full-utterance recordings and source English remain unchanged. These are draft introductions, not verified native morphology, invented word recordings, a grammar engine, or evidence of mastered knowledge.

entries.cue: Poproszę is a polite way to ask for something. Wodę means water as the thing you are requesting; practise the complete sentence.
Poproszę introduces the request; kawę is coffee in the form used after this request. Compare it with Poproszę wodę.
Herbatę means tea when requested here. Poproszę remains the same while the requested drink changes.
Zupa means soup; dnia means of the day. Zupa dnia is the common full menu phrase soup of the day.
Deser is dessert. This is a standalone noun here, so learn the complete recorded word and its meaning.
Ile asks how much. To means this or it; kosztuje means costs. Together Ile to kosztuje? asks how much this costs.
Ile ...? asks how much, while razem means together or altogether. Compare this with Ile to kosztuje?.
Czy introduces the yes/no question. Mogę means can I, zapłacić means to pay, and kartą means by card.
Gdzie asks where, jest means is, and kasa is the checkout or cash desk. The question follows the Gdzie jest ...? pattern.
Poproszę makes this polite. Paragon means a receipt; use the whole expression when asking for one.
Gdzie jest ...? asks where something is. Przystanek is a stop for a bus or tram; here you ask where the stop is.
Gdzie jest ...? is the same where-is question. Metro names the subway or metro system.
Ile means how much, kosztuje means costs, and bilet means ticket. Notice that the price question differs from Ile to kosztuje?.

entries.english: Where can I buy a ticket?
entries.cue: Gdzie means where; mogę means can I; kupić means buy; bilet means ticket. Practise the complete Where can I buy a ticket? question.
Czy starts a yes/no question. To means it or this, daleko means far, and stąd means from here.
